content.title: Two-Phase Structured Extraction for Complex Technical Documents
content.use_cases: Applies when processing complex technical documents (e.g., equipment specs, engineering standards) that contain OCR errors, chapter numbering gaps, duplicate/conflicting tables, and non-extractable image content. Triggered when user requests structured JSON output from documents with known quality issues, especially when completeness and traceability are critical.
content.hints: Phase 1: Generate a self_review artifact covering dimensions like coverage, omissions, format issues, and granularity. Flag specific problems (typos, duplicate section numbers, table conflicts, image limitations) with next_actions. Phase 2: Execute next_actions systematically, embedding audit annotations directly into corresponding JSON fields (e.g., in a 'notes' or '指标特征' field) rather than outputting them separately — this preserves traceability without cluttering the main output. Always include a __META__ block explicitly noting unextractable content (images, ASCII diagrams) to prevent downstream consumers from assuming data completeness. If user specifies output constraints ('only JSON, no explanatory text'), strictly honor them from Phase 2 onward. This two-phase approach reduces omission risk versus single-pass processing of complex documents.

content.title: Inline Annotation of Document Quality Issues in Structured Output
content.use_cases: Applies when converting technical documents with known defects (OCR errors, duplicate entries, conflicting table data, missing sections) into structured JSON. The goal is to maintain quality traceability without producing a separate error report that may be ignored or lost.
content.hints: Embed quality annotations (typo corrections, conflicts, extraction failures) directly into the relevant JSON field rather than appending a separate error list. For example, note '液氨→液氮 (typo corrected)' inside the field value or a dedicated annotation subfield. For duplicate table entries with differing values, record both values and flag the discrepancy inline. This approach keeps the JSON self-documenting and auditable. Reserve __META__ for document-level limitations (e.g., 'Section X contains images that could not be parsed'). Avoid silently dropping problematic fields — always represent them with a note.
